content.section_a_high_risk_definition: One of the following clinical presentations: cardiac arrest; obstructive shock defined as systolic BP <90 mmHg or vasopressors required to achieve a BP ≥90 mmHg despite adequate filling status in combination with end-organ hypoperfusion; or persistent hypotension defined as systolic BP <90 mmHg or a systolic BP drop ≥40 mmHg for >15 min not due to new-onset arrhythmia, hypovolaemia, or sepsis.
content.section_b_imaging: Prognostically relevant imaging (transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) or CTPA) findings in patients with acute PE and corresponding cut-off levels are presented in Figure 3 and summarized in Supplementary Data Table 3.
content.section_c_biomarkers: Elevation of laboratory biomarkers (may provide additional prognostic information) including NT-proBNP ≥600 ng/L, H-FABP ≥6 ng/mL, or copeptin ≥24 pmol/L. These markers have been validated in cohort studies but not used to guide treatment decisions in randomized controlled trials.
content.section_d_hemodynamic_instability: Haemodynamic instability combined with PE confirmation on CTPA and/or evidence of RV dysfunction on TTE is sufficient to classify a patient into the high-risk PE category. In these cases calculation of the PESI nor measurement of troponins or other cardiac biomarkers is necessary.
content.section_e_risk_stratification_intermedia: Signs of RV dysfunction on TTE (or CTPA) or elevated cardiac biomarker levels may be present despite a low PESI class or sPESI of 0. Until implications are fully understood these patients should be classified into the intermediate-risk category. Further risk stratification is recommended in absence of haemodynamic instability because it has implications for early discharge vs hospitalization/monitoring. Patients in the intermediate-risk group who display both RV dysfunction (echocardiography or CTPA) and elevated cardiac biomarkers (particularly a positive cardiac troponin test) are classified as intermediate–high-risk; close monitoring is recommended to detect haemodynamic decompensation.
content.notes_references_tables_figures: References to Figure 3, Supplementary Data Table 3, and Table 8 for detailed cut-offs and overview of clinical, imaging, and laboratory parameters used to distinguish intermediate- and low-risk PE. PESI (original or simplified) is highlighted as the most extensively validated clinical score for predicting low-risk PE.
